claim: S&P Global flash US Services PMI surged to 56.8 in August 2026 (a 20-month high, up from 54.6 in July), signaling strong services-sector expansion momentum heading into the ISM release.

Continuum Economics, in its pre-release preview, explicitly forecasts an August ISM Services reading of 54.5, above the market consensus of 54.3, citing the index remaining 'slightly firmer within a tight range.'
July 2026 ISM services new orders (57.2%) and business activity (59.1%) both printed well above the headline index, providing strong positive carry-over demand momentum into August.
S&P Global estimates Q3 2026 annualized GDP growth near 3.0%, nearly double Q2's 1.5% pace, indicating broad economic resilience that is typically consistent with above-trend ISM services readings.

ADP private-sector employment rose by only 38,000 in August 2026 (slowest since January), with professional and business services shedding 16,000 jobs, pointing to a continued or deepening contraction in the already-depressed ISM services employment sub-index (47.4% in July).

Regional Fed services surveys from the Philadelphia, Richmond, and Empire State Feds all slowed in August 2026, providing a cross-check that partially offsets the bullish signal from the S&P Global flash PMI.
The S&P Global services PMI is 'not well correlated with ISM services' per Continuum Economics, meaning the flash PMI surge to 56.8 has limited predictive power for the ISM headline reading.

The ISM services prices paid index re-accelerated to 70.3% in July 2026 (its highest in years), creating margin compression pressures for service-sector businesses that could dampen activity and new orders in August.

The S&P Global flash manufacturing PMI fell to a 13-month low of 53.2 in August, driven in part by supply disruptions linked to the US-led conflict with Iran, a shock that could spill into services-sector supply chains and cost structures.
